result.summary: This PR removes two convenience methods, btck_chain_get_genesis and btck_chain_get_tip, from the kernel's C++ wrapper (bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h), since both are trivially replaceable with btck_chain_get_by_height. The author argues neither removal is a regression because master never guaranteed the returned block index still corresponds to the actual tip anyway.
result.problem: The Chain interface in the kernel wrapper carries two methods that duplicate functionality already available via btck_chain_get_by_height, adding surface area to an API that kernel maintainers want to keep minimal and well-defined.

resolved_concerns: TheCharlatan raised whether the thread-safety property of the old Tip/Genesis calls is worth preserving; author and TheCharlatan agreed the property is marginal/theoretical and the calls should just be removed.
maflcko noted a rare reorg edge case where get_by_height could throw; author acknowledged it as an existing, unsolved reorg-safety issue elsewhere in the interface, not a blocker.

reviewability.label: Ready
reviewability.reason: No mechanical blockers and no open material question; the thread-safety and reorg-edge-case points raised were discussed and resolved as non-blocking by all participants.

agreement.summary: Strong support: yuvicc ACKed and TheCharlatan gave Concept ACK, agreeing the removed methods' benefit is marginal and not worth keeping.
agreement.reason: Two reviewers explicitly support removal with stated reasoning (marginal thread-safety benefit, redundancy with get_by_height), and no one objects to the change itself.
evidence: yuvicc: 'ACK ... This makes sense to me.'
TheCharlatan: 'Concept ACK ... their benefit (thread safety) is kind of marginal.'
TheCharlatan later: 'External callers should provide synchronization for this. So the two calls should just be removed imo.'

enables: author mentions a follow-up PR generalizing Range objects as the sole public interface for chain contents, to be pushed out soon

categories.name: kernel
categories.evidence: Directly modifies src/kernel/bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h, removing two public API methods from the kernel's C++ wrapper interface.
categories.rationale: This is API polish removing redundant methods with no stated external consumer depending on them, per bands.md rubric this is P3-P4 territory. It slightly reduces surface area for the kernel API but the discussion itself calls the removed thread-safety guarantee 'marginal' and 'theoretical', so there's no real correctness or usability gain being claimed. It may set up further cleanup (author mentions a follow-up PR reworking Range objects), giving it minor leverage.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: The PR only touches the kernel wrapper header, not validation logic, chainstate management, or block/transaction acceptance rules. The Validation label appears to be applied because kernel wraps validation-adjacent concepts, but per the validation category definition, kernel-API-only changes belong to kernel, not validation.
categories.rationale: No validation logic (block/tx acceptance, chainstate, UTXO set, reorg handling) is changed; this is purely a kernel wrapper API trim, so it does not meet the validation category's substantive-change bar despite the Validation label.

uncertainties: Whether the 'Validation' label reflects an intentional maintainer categorization decision that should override my read that this is kernel-only; treated it as likely mislabeling since the diff is confined to the kernel wrapper header.
result.card: This PR removes two methods, btck_chain_get_genesis and btck_chain_get_tip, from the kernel's C++ wrapper interface (bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h), arguing they are redundant with btck_chain_get_by_height and provide no real regression since neither guaranteed actual-tip correspondence on master. Reviewers yuvicc and TheCharlatan both support removal, agreeing the thread-safety benefit of the old methods was marginal; maflcko raised a rare reorg edge case that the author acknowledged as an existing unrelated issue, not a blocker. The PR is small, fully discussed, and ready for merge-focused review. It touches only the kernel API surface, not validation logic itself, despite carrying the Validation label. No dependencies block it, though the author mentions a related follow-up PR reworking Range objects is coming.
